questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A glacier dated by the rubble in front of it
questions.learningObjective: explain how a landform is dated and what the date covers
questions.stem: A valley glacier has retreated a long way from the walls of its valley, and a ridge of angular rock lies in front of it in several places, with soil and plants colonising the surface of the ridge. A study dates the ridge by one of the methods available for exposed rock and dates a sample of wood from a tree growing on the ridge. Which statement about the two dates is best supported?

options.text: The ridge and the wood give the same date, since a tree cannot grow on a deposit older than the deposit
options.misconception: assumes the tree dated the surface it is standing on

options.text: The ridge is a deposit left at the ice front, so its date is a minimum for the ice's retreat past that point, and the wood on top gives only an age for the tree
The ridge is a deposit left at the ice front, so its date is the date the glacier last stood there, and the vegetation on it shows the retreat has now stopped
options.misconception: reads a present state from a date of deposition

options.text: Neither date is a date of the ice, since rock transported by ice records the transport and not the moment of deposition
options.misconception: supplies a general objection that applies to moraines and to nothing else

questions.explanation: A moraine is a specific sort of evidence and the strength of the case depends on being clear about which question it answers. The rubble was dropped by the ice when the ice stood at that point, so the deposit's date is the date the ice was there, and since the ice front moved afterwards, that date is a minimum for how far the front has retreated and a maximum for when the retreat began. The vegetation is a separate matter: plants colonise rock and stabilise it, so a well-developed soil and a mature tree show that the surface has been stable for a long time, and the age of the tree is evidence about the tree, not about the deposit beneath it. The distinction matters in practice, because a deposit dated by the rock and a tree dated by its rings are routinely reported as though they dated the same event, and the difference between them can be centuries.
questions.hint: Ask what each of the two things is a proxy for, and whether they are the same kind of evidence.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A soil read as a sequence
questions.learningObjective: interpret an accumulating soil as a record of successive conditions
questions.stem: At an abandoned settlement a digger's face shows, from the top: a modern ploughsoil, a dark band rich in charcoal and refuse, a pale band of loose sand, then a buried surface with the remains of plants growing on it. Which feature of the section carries the most information about the order of events?

options.text: The buried surface, since material lying on it must have been deposited after it formed and before the sand covered it, which fixes the sequence of the three conditions above it
The charcoal band, since charcoal is always the remains of a fire and therefore always marks a destruction
options.misconception: infers an event from a material that can arrive by several routes

options.text: The ploughsoil, since its depth measures how long the land has been farmed after the abandonment
options.misconception: treats a thickness as a clock with no relation to deposition

options.text: The pale sand, since sand is laid down by wind and therefore the section records a period of aridity
options.misconception: assigns a depositional agent from the grain size alone

questions.explanation: The whole reading of a section like this rests on the principle that what lies on a surface is later than the surface, which turns a vertical face into a sequence of horizontal moments. The buried surface is the most informative level because it is a moment rather than a material: plants grew on it, so it was a land surface, and the charcoal and the sand above it are both later than that moment, which orders them and anchors the rest. The three distractors each read a material as though it named a single process, which is the standing temptation with a section. Charcoal can come from a hearth, a fire or a distant burn washed down; sand can be wind, a river or a deliberate fill; and a ploughsoil's depth is governed by how long the plough has been going over it and how much material the plough brings up, not by a rate that can be converted into years. Reading a section is a matter of proposing processes and then looking for the things that would refute them.
questions.hint: Ask which level is a moment rather than a material, and what must be later than it.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A harvest record and what it is a proxy for
questions.learningObjective: assess an indirect indicator of climate and its limits
questions.stem: A region's surviving records note the date on which grapes were picked in each year over several centuries, and a study treats that date as an index of summer conditions. Which limitation of the series is most important to state?

options.text: The record is a proxy for the region's wine, so it says nothing about harvests of grain and the two can move independently
options.misconception: turns a regional limit into a claim that the series is worthless

options.text: The record cannot be a proxy at all, since only measurements of temperature can bear on climate and an administrative entry is not one
options.misconception: rules out a whole class of historical indicator

options.text: The record is a proxy for the growers' decisions rather than for the summer itself, and the decisions depend on labour, law, markets and custom as well as on the weather
The record is a sound proxy, since the date of picking is set by the fruit and therefore varies only with the season
options.misconception: assumes a single cause governs the recorded decision

questions.explanation: An indirect indicator is valuable precisely because it exists where direct measurement does not, and it is also always a measurement of something that somebody did. The date on which a crop was gathered reflects the state of the crop, and the state of the crop reflects the summer, but the day chosen also reflects what the law required, what the labour was available for, what the last buyer would take, and what was done in the twenty years before. None of that is noise to be averaged out, because the customs do not fall on the same years for everyone. What makes such a series usable anyway is that the practice varies slowly compared with the weather, so a shift in the practice is visible as a level change in a record of several centuries, and the short-run variation can be read against the long-run trend. The honest statement of the limit is therefore not that the series is bad but that it measures a decision, and that the decision is one climate-shaped thing among several.
questions.hint: Ask what the person writing the date was actually recording, and what else decided it.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A warning system and the decision it does not make
questions.learningObjective: distinguish what a forecasting system does from the policy that follows from it
questions.stem: An organisation maintains a system that forecasts the appearance of a migratory insect pest from rainfall over its breeding grounds, holds the observations of a network of local reporters, and issues bulletins when the risk rises. Treatment of the breeding areas has to be authorised and paid for by governments. Which feature of the arrangement limits what the forecasting system can achieve?

options.text: The system has no authority to act, which is why the observation network must be expanded until the forecast is certain
options.misconception: supposes that a better forecast removes the need for a decision

options.text: The system produces information and the decisions and resources are made elsewhere, so a forecast can be right and still produce no treatment
The system is redundant, since the insects can be seen and counted directly in the district they threaten
options.misconception: denies the value of advance notice before an invasion

options.text: The system is ineffective, since the insects travel faster than any bulletin can be issued
options.misconception: asserts a speed comparison the case gives no basis for

questions.explanation: This is the ordinary shape of an informational system attached to a decision system, and the gap between them is where most of the disappointment lives. A forecast can be accurate, early and useless if the action it recommends requires money that has to be approved, a rule that has to be invoked, a season that has to be right and a government that has to accept that the risk is real. Forecasting therefore raises rather than reduces the value of a decision procedure, since a warning creates an obligation to decide and a deadline by which the decision must be made, and an organisation that has announced a risk and then done nothing has made things worse for itself. The historical interest of such a system lies in its records: a long series of forecasts and outcomes is one of the few places where the quality of a prediction can be measured rather than asserted, and such series are consequently worth preserving as evidence.
questions.hint: Ask who has to act on the bulletin, and where the authority to act actually lies.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A warning that arrives after the rains that produced it
questions.learningObjective: explain the structural lag in a forecast built on rainfall observations
questions.stem: A forecasting system for a migratory insect pest infers its behaviour from rainfall over the deserts in which the pest breeds. The rains that make a breeding area suitable also make it hard to reach, and the insects begin to multiply as soon as the rains allow. Which feature of that arrangement is the structural difficulty for the forecaster?

options.text: The insects breed too quickly for any observation to be useful, since a generation takes less time than a report can be written
options.misconception: asserts a speed that the arrangement does not require

options.text: The forecasters lack the means to observe rainfall accurately, since deserts have no instruments
options.misconception: supplies a technical failure where the difficulty is a delay

options.text: The forecast is reliable only for the year it was made, since the breeding areas change from season to season in ways nobody models
options.misconception: concedes unpredictability the arrangement does not imply

options.text: The conditions that create the risk are also the conditions that delay the news of it, so the information arrives after the population has already multiplied

questions.explanation: The difficulty is a structural lag, and it is worth being precise about where it sits, because a lag of this kind cannot be engineered away by better observation. The information is about a remote surface, it travels by road and by radio, and it is generated by the same rainfall that is making the roads impassable and the population multiplying. By the time a bulletin arrives the risk is not a possibility but an established population, and the action that would have been cheap at the first stage of multiplication, treating a limited area, is by the reporting stage an operation over a large distance. The consequence for the system is that its value lies in the second and third breeding cycles rather than the first, which is also why an organisation that reports risk and is not heard is in a worse position than one that never reported, because the decision has been publicly required and visibly not taken.
questions.hint: Ask what has to happen locally for the observation that the forecast depends on to exist.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A regulation that outlived the disease it was made for
questions.learningObjective: trace what happens to an apparatus after the emergency that justified it
questions.stem: A colonial administration passes laws requiring the inspection, the marking and the movement control of livestock, and creates a veterinary service to enforce them, during a decade in which a cattle disease kills most of the herds. The disease is later driven out of the country, and the laws and the service remain. Which consequence of that sequence is most likely to be studied?

options.text: The apparatus is dissolved with the emergency, so the later history of the service is a record of orderly demobilisation
options.misconception: assumes that a legal instrument expires with the event that prompted it

options.text: The laws are repealed, and the interest lies in the resistance of the people they governed during the decade of the disease
options.misconception: puts the end of the laws before the disease was over

options.text: The apparatus of control outlives its occasion, and the interesting history afterwards is the one in which the rules were applied to animals, trades and movements that the emergency had never been about
The service is retained for the prevention of a later disease, so its later history belongs to the history of that disease rather than to this one
options.misconception: assumes a purpose the sequence does not state

questions.explanation: Emergency institutions are unusually durable, and the reason is structural rather than sentimental: a legal instrument creates posts, a budget, a reporting line and a body of trained people, and all four survive the emergency that justified them, while the reason for the apparatus is no longer present to argue for its dissolution. That is why the history after the emergency is usually the more interesting half, and it is generally not a story about the disease at all. A veterinary service built to control a plague in cattle ends up regulating the movement of animals, the licensing of trades, the inspection of markets and the certification of products for export, and each of those uses gives the organisation a constituency that wants it to continue. This is a general pattern in state formation, and the pairing to look for is always the same: what does the apparatus now do, and who benefits from it doing that.
questions.hint: Ask what the apparatus does once the reason for building it has passed.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: The reservoir a second eradication worried about
questions.learningObjective: explain why a disease confined to people is a different problem from one with an animal reservoir
questions.stem: A campaign against a disease of domestic animals reached its final years with no human cases at all, and the officials responsible for certifying the result spent their last years looking for the organism in wild animals, in the herds at the edge of the settled area, and in the laboratory methods used to detect a low-level presence. Which feature of that final phase is best explained by the biology of the organism?

options.text: The organism survives in wild animals of several species, so it can persist where nobody is looking, and certifying an absence requires methods sensitive enough to find a very low level
The organism cannot survive outside domestic animals, so the final years were spent on a possibility that the biology had already excluded
options.misconception: assumes a single host when the campaign's purpose implied otherwise

options.text: The organism requires warmth, so the final years were spent on a search bounded by latitude rather than by detection
options.misconception: reduces the search to one physical limit and leaves the rest unexplained

options.text: The organism decays quickly outside the body, so the final years were spent on establishing how long a trace could survive
options.misconception: asserts a decay rate the sequence does not give

questions.explanation: The shape of the last phase of this campaign is set by the host range, and the reason it needed laboratory methods is the same reason it needed the wild animals at all. If the organism can persist in several species of wild ungulate, then an eradication that has cleared the domestic population has not removed the organism, it has removed the population in which it was being noticed. What remains is a sampling problem of a hard kind, since the animal in question is not rare but is hard to catch, so the design of any survey has to assume that a low level of presence will look identical to absence unless the detection method is good enough to say otherwise. That is why the final years of such a campaign are spent on detection rather than on treatment, and it is a useful corrective to the way these achievements are usually told, as a sequence of dramatic interventions rather than as a long argument with an invisible population.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A campaign office as a records office
questions.learningObjective: explain why an administrative campaign produces unusually valuable evidence
questions.stem: A vaccination campaign's district offices were required to keep returns of doses given, lists of persons vaccinated, notifications of cases, and a monthly summary sent upward. A research institute later obtained the raw monthly returns and found that they could be used to map the spread of the disease month by month in a way the published reports did not attempt. Which feature of the returns makes them more useful than the reports?

options.text: The returns were written by scientists, so they are more accurate than the reports written by officials
options.misconception: attributes quality to the profession of the writer rather than to the purpose of the record

options.text: The reports summarise the returns, so the returns must be more detailed and the difference is one of condensation
options.misconception: supposes a difference of length where there is a difference of purpose

options.text: The returns are raw, so the figures have not yet been checked by anybody and are therefore closer to the truth
options.misconception: treats the absence of editing as the presence of accuracy

options.text: The returns were made for a fixed administrative purpose by people who had to be consistent with the next month's return, so an error has to repeat itself to survive

questions.explanation: The value of an administrative series lies in a property that sounds trivial and is not, which is that somebody had to reconcile it with itself and with the next one. A district officer sending a monthly return is not writing history and has no reason to improve on a figure, but he does have a reason to be consistent, because the district's own totals are compared with the province's and an unexplained jump invites a question he would rather not be asked. That consistency is a built-in check on the kind of error that a single document cannot detect, and it is why the raw returns of an administration frequently support finer analysis than the reports written from them. The fourth option states the error neatly: an unedited figure is not thereby a truer one, since the errors that survive in administrative records are usually systematic, which is exactly the sort that repeated reporting exposes.
questions.hint: Ask what the officer had to do with last month's return before he could send this one.

questions.topic: A curve drawn through a shock
questions.learningObjective: assess the effect of smoothing on a mortality series
questions.stem: A country's population over a century is plotted as a smooth line, and the line shows a gentle rise interrupted by a rounded dip. The same data plotted as annual figures shows that the fall took place in a single year, that two successive years were the lowest of the century, and that the population was higher within a decade than the trend line had predicted. Which feature of the smoothed version is most likely to mislead a reader?

options.misconception: supposes that averaging alters a level rather than a shape

options.misconception: declares the rendering useless rather than limiting

options.text: The smoothing conceals a rise, since the line never goes up sharply enough to show a recovery
options.misconception: invents a missing movement in a line that plainly contains one

questions.explanation: A smoothed line answers a question about the trend and hides the question about the event, and the choice between the two is a choice about what the reader needs. Averaging across a few years is exactly right for asking how the level of a population has changed over decades, because the short-run variation is noise for that purpose. It is exactly wrong for asking what a specific decade was like, and the information destroyed is not cosmetic: an abrupt fall lasting one or two years points to an event with a cause and a date, while the same years expressed as a rounded dip can equally well be produced by several small declines spread across a decade. The comparison with the trend line makes the point, since a population that recovered within a decade of a sharp shock has a very different history from one that merely resumed a slow growth, and only the unsmoothed data can tell the two apart.
questions.hint: Ask what the annual figures show that the rounded dip cannot show.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: Explaining a region's fate by its climate
questions.learningObjective: evaluate an environmental explanation of the distribution of a region's achievement
questions.stem: A nineteenth-century argument held that the peoples of a hot and humid region were made less energetic and less capable of political organisation than those of a temperate one, and that this explained why that region had not produced states or science, while a temperate region had. The argument was used to explain the distribution of achievement in a way that assigned the difference to the people rather than to their circumstances. Which objection is best supported?

options.text: The argument is sound in outline, since a climate that makes work difficult will produce less of certain kinds of work, and the distribution of achievement is a fact that needs explaining
options.misconception: accepts the inference from a condition to a capacity without objecting to it

options.text: The argument is unsound only in its details, since the climate it invokes is measurable and the measurements are the part that is imprecise
options.misconception: reduces a conceptual objection to a complaint about data

options.text: The argument takes a feature of a climate and treats it as a fixed property of a people, and it does so in a way that makes the distribution it claims to explain a property of the people rather than a result of conditions, institutions and choices
The argument is unsound because the region it describes had in fact produced states and science, so the premise is contradicted by the record
options.misconception: answers the argument with a counter-example rather than with the structure of the inference

questions.explanation: The argument fails at two points that have to be kept apart, because the second is the more serious one. The first is that a climate is treated as an influence on a population's capacity, which is a claim about a group's fixed characteristics that the argument never earns and that it is entitled to earn only from its own evidence. The second and deeper point is the direction of the explanation: the distribution of achievement is used as the observation to be explained, and the explanation is then built so that the people are assigned the cause of what happened to them, which makes the outcome into a property of the group and forecloses the questions that would actually explain it. A fourth option is not a good answer, because a single counter-example refutes a general claim only if the general claim is about the specific case; the argument here is about a region, and the existence of achievement somewhere in a region is consistent with any account of the distribution.
questions.hint: Ask what the explanation makes the outcome a property of.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: An explanation in which the affected people cannot choose
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a structural account from one that excludes agency
questions.stem: Two accounts of the same sequence are offered. The first says that a region's poverty, isolation and dependence on a single export left its people few options, and that the sequence followed from those constraints together with decisions taken by people who chose among the options available. The second says that the sequence followed from the environment, and that the people of the region appear in it as the objects of what happened to them. Which statement about the pair is soundest?

options.text: The first account is compatible with strong constraint, since a choice among very few options is still a choice, and the second is an account of the same facts in which the people have become a description rather than an agent
The two accounts are opposites, so the second is correct whenever the first is, since an account that mentions choice cannot be right about an outcome nobody chose
options.misconception: makes the presence of agency decisive against structural constraint

options.text: The two accounts are opposites, so the first is a moral argument dressed as a historical one and the second is the more rigorous
options.misconception: judges a question of evidence by the tone of the prose

options.text: The two accounts are the same account, since a constraint is only a condition and a decision is only a choice between conditions
options.misconception: collapses a distinction the two accounts are actually making

questions.explanation: The distinction being tested is the difference between a strong account of constraint and an account that has removed the people from the story, and the two are easy to confuse because the second is usually written in the vocabulary of the first. Constraint and agency are not opposites, since a decision is a selection among available options and the set of available options is precisely what an account of constraint is describing; the interesting historical work lies in establishing how narrow the set was in each case and what happened to the people who refused. What the second account does is subtler than a simple omission: it retains the people as a condition in an argument, which is why it reads as explanation while removing the possibility that anything they did mattered, and why its predictions are unfalsifiable, since every outcome the region produces can then be read back as the expression of the environment. That is the practical test for telling the two kinds of account apart.
questions.hint: Ask whether the people in the second account could have done anything that would have changed the sequence.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A note recording a decision not to intervene
questions.learningObjective: read an administrative note as evidence about a decision and its reasons

stimulus.body: A note written by a district officer and initialled by the commissioner, found among the papers of a later inquiry: 'I have the returns of the three districts before me and they do not show a failure of the harvest. The deaths reported in the fourth district are in the same proportion to its population as those of the three, and its price is the same. I am therefore of the opinion that no relief is warranted, and I recommend that the grain be held where it is until the returns of the coming month. If the commissioner thinks a private supply should be sent on his own authority, he will do so, and I will not be responsible.'
stimulus.license: original text written for this bank; no protected source reproduced

questions.stem: Read the note. Which statement about it is best supported?

options.text: The note records a refusal of responsibility rather than a judgement, since the officer's disagreement with the commissioner is the substance of the note
options.misconception: treats the transfer of responsibility as the whole content of a reasoned judgement

options.text: The note records a decision with reasons, and the reason given is a comparison of rates rather than an inspection, so the decision rests on the figures being comparable across the four districts
The note shows that the district's people did not need relief, since an officer who had visited the villages would have known otherwise
options.misconception: supplies a visit the note does not mention and an officer's omniscience

options.text: The note shows that the commissioner was minded to intervene for political reasons, since an officer would not oppose him over figures alone
options.misconception: infers a motive for the superior from the disagreement the note records

questions.explanation: The note is a small, ordinary document and it can be read in two ways, which makes it a good exercise. What it certainly contains is a decision, a reason, and a delegation upward, and the reason is a comparison: three districts show no failure and the fourth's deaths and prices are in the same proportion, so the fourth is not distinguishable from the others on those measures. That reasoning is sound in form and it depends entirely on the comparability of the four returns, which is the thing a reader should press, since a district with a denser reporting system produces more counted deaths and a district with a better market shows more prices. What the note does not contain is any information about who within the district was dying, and the passage of time between the returns and the deaths is left open by the recommendation itself, since a decision to wait for the next month's returns is a decision to accept a delay.
questions.hint: Ask what the officer compared, and what the comparison assumes about the four districts.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A census taken in a year of catastrophe
questions.learningObjective: assess a population count collected under extraordinary conditions
questions.stem: An administration conducts its decennial enumeration in a year of high mortality, displacement and flight, and publishes a population figure that is used for thirty years as the denominator of every rate calculated from the period. Which feature of the enumeration most threatens its use as a denominator?

options.text: The count is taken too frequently, so a decennial figure cannot capture the population between two enumerations
options.misconception: objects to a frequency the case describes as a strength

options.text: The count is taken by officials of the same administration that is distributing relief, so the number is politically motivated
options.misconception: supplies a motive the case gives no evidence for

options.text: The count is taken before the year's deaths are complete, so the figure understates the population of the following year
options.misconception: assumes a timing of the enumeration the case does not state

options.text: The count is taken at a moment when the population is unusually mobile and unusually reduced, so the number recorded is not representative of the population of the decade it is used to describe

questions.explanation: A denominator is a statement about a population on a particular day, and a rate is that day's population used to standardise a count of events spread across years. When the day in question is unusual, the standardisation is distorted in a direction that depends on the kind of unusualness, and here both kinds are present: mortality has reduced the count, and displacement has redistributed it, so the enumerated figure is both too low for the year before and badly distributed between one district and the next. The practical consequences run for a generation, since every per-capita figure for the decade inherits the error, and a district that lost people will show a spuriously high rate for the whole period while a district that received them shows a spuriously low one. The habit worth forming is to ask of any long-used denominator when it was counted and what was happening then, before reading a single rate that rests on it.
questions.hint: Ask what the day of the enumeration looked like, and what a rate built on it inherits.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.topic: A claim that a measure prevented a collapse
questions.learningObjective: assess a counterfactual claim about a preventive measure
questions.stem: A review of a public health measure introduced in one country during a bad harvest year concludes that the measure prevented a famine, since the deaths recorded in the districts that received it were low while those in the districts that did not were high. A critic replies that the districts which received relief were chosen for being the poorer ones, so the comparison is between places that were not alike, and that the deaths of the poorer districts would have been high in any case. Which statement about the pair is soundest?

options.text: The review's comparison is between districts that differed before the measure, so the difference in deaths is consistent with the relief having had no effect, and settling it requires comparing a treated place with a similar untreated one
The critic is right that the districts differed, and the review is right that relief was effective, since a measure can only lower deaths in the places that were worst off to begin with
options.misconception: concedes the selection and draws the opposite conclusion from it

options.text: The dispute is unresolvable, since no relief programme leaves any place untreated for a counterfactual to be found in
options.misconception: rules out the comparison that historical work of this kind does

options.text: The review is right and the critic is wrong, since the relief was distributed by a rule and a rule cannot select the worse-off by accident
options.misconception: assumes that a rule operates independently of the sorting it is applied to

questions.explanation: The review has made the classic error of a comparison that runs backwards in time: it compares places with one another after the treatment was assigned, when the assignment itself was selective. A rule that sends relief to the poorest districts is a rule that sorts, so the treated and untreated groups differ before the measure as well as after, and a difference in outcomes between them is exactly what one expects even if the measure did nothing at all. The critic is therefore right about the structure of the comparison and wrong to call the matter closed, because the structure has a cure. A randomised allocation is unavailable retrospectively, but a difference in differences can be built from a period before the measure, from a measure of outcome less sensitive to the selection, or from a comparison among places treated at different times, and each of those is a way of manufacturing the untreated group that the review lacks.
questions.hint: Ask whether the treated and untreated places were alike before the measure, and how one would find out.
